messages.subject: How to plot sub-region out of a region (eg. plot Malaysia and Singapore in the same map)?
parts:
Dear all,

I am really new to R and have been reading the cookbook these days to get started. However, I have a task to solve for the moment and I figure that I could not catch up quick enough.

Please anyone could provide some help and advise. Thanks!

The task:

The first part of task is to plot countries(and regions) in a map. However, ggplot doesn't recognize Singapore, HK and Taiwan as a region. What I tried is to create a layer just for these three regions, with lat and long, on top of region layer, but I got stuck with the code. Could anyone help??

btw, why all the codes I typed in R is black. In other languages I see green read etc to differentiate certain type of codes. How to do it in R?


library(ggplot2)
map.world <- map_data(map = "world")

# clip Antarctica. Nobody wants to see Antarctica
map.world2 <- subset(map.world, !region == "Antarctica")

p1 <- ggplot(map.world2, aes(x = long, y = lat))
p1 <- p1 + geom_polygon(fill = grey(0.8), aes(group = group))
#print(p1)

# Example map using the countries of the financial centers data set:
map2 <- subset(map.world2, region %in% c("USA","Germany","France"
,"Italy","Japan","Australia","China","Netherlands"
,"South Korea","UK","Canada","Belgium","New Zealand", "Malaysia","Greece"
,"South Africa","Bulgaria","Hong Kong","Singapore","Taiwan")
)
p1 <- p1 + geom_path(aes(x = long
    , y = lat, group = group, color = region),data = map2, size = 1)
p1 <- p1 + theme(legend.position="none")

print(p1)
